author: amenes12
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD041 -->

<!--
Before you start, please make sure your issue is understandable and reproducible.
To make your issue readable make sure you use valid Markdown syntax.
https://guides.github.com/features/mastering-markdown/
-->

### What does it do

Implements CRUD actions (create, read, update, delete) for Companies endpoint in our API.

### Usage

Endpoint: `/api/v1/companies`

- Make GET requests to list all the existing companies in the repository
- Make POST requests to create a new company.

Endpoint: `/api/v1/companies/{id}`
- Make PUT requests to update an existing company in the repository with the specified ID in the endpoint.
- Make PATCH requests to partially update an existing company in the repository with the specified ID in the endpoint.
- Make DELETE requests to delete an existing company in the repository with the specified ID in the endpoint.

### Why is it needed

Our client needs to manage registered companies.

author: crummel
body: In the installer tarball build, we want to remove the `objects` directories from the .gitdirs in order to save space and allow the tarball to be checked into a Git repo itself.  This causes a problem in the specific configuration of a submodule with a redirected .gitdir where the `objects` directory has been deleted - Git will error out attempting to apply patches from that current directory.  This introduces a workaround by setting GIT_DIR to /dev/null, so Git will skip .gitdir discovery and instead treat the submodule directory like any other non-source-controlled directory.  This is acceptable because we just need the patches to be applied.

##### SUMMARY

On devel, unreachable hosts pick up where they left off.

On this branch, unreachable hosts pick up at the next play.

I'm not sure if this is the right behavior, because ~I can imagine content relying on the behavior of devel (it's the only mechanism to recover an unreachable host, and it could be intuitive using the free strategy), and~ people using the linear strategy could expect the host should start at the task following the next applicable task following the clear_host_errors task instead of the next play.

body: Add manually release workflow that can be triggered via the Github actions interface. See https://github.com/OAK-Foundation/ci-blockchain/actions/workflows/release.yml for example runs: * https://github.com/OAK-Foundation/ci-blockchain/actions/runs/2506172789 with Runtime WASM build * https://github.com/OAK-Foundation/ci-blockchain/actions/runs/2536846279 with Debian Package This will: * Build the Rust binary using our self-hosted runner * Build a Debian package * Build the WASM runtime using srtool in a Github hosted runner * Build the Docker image by copying the built Rust binary and upload it to Docker hub * Generate a draft release with appropriate notes and attach built artifacts This does not create the git tag and requires it to manually generated before release. author: sevaa
body:
The changes to the ranges section format are close in spirit to those that they did to loclists (see #418) , but not as drastic. There are no CU headers.

Instead of fixed format records with magic values, range list entries are now stored as prefixed with type (`DW_RLE`), with several possible encodings for each kind, so storing both entry address and entry length became necessary for readelf dumping.

I saw range lists overlapping - one `DW_AT_ranges` pointing in the middle of a range list that was referenced in some other `DW_AT_ranges`. GNU readelf handles that gracefully, so we had to. The preexisting logic of RangeLists.iter_range_lists() didn't accommodate for that, so I changed it to scan all DIEs for `DW_AT_ranges` values and scrolling through those.

The indirect encodings are not supported, just like with loclists. **I could try and debug that on my clang-11 binary, but no autotest until we upgrade readelf. Should I?**

FYI, the tag 2.38 is present in the binutils' sources...

author: cuducos
body:
My first attemp to use [`tokio`](https://tokio.rs/). The idea is to process each file passed to `grrs` asynchronously. E.g.:

```
$ grrs 42 /tmp/guide.txt /tmp/whatever.txt
```

This command would spawn two async workers, one for `/tmp/guide.txt` and another for `/tmp/whatever.txt`. The output order may vary as a consequence — but still must include the name of the file before listing its lines with matches.

author: ymorimo
body:
This PR adds a provisioned Grafana dashboard JSON configuration file for the GraphQL Prometheus metrics.

Please note that this PR is built on top of #110.

---

## Example installation steps on minikube

### Start Cassandra and load the emoney schema

```console
docker run -d --rm --name cassandra-scalardb --network minikube -p 9042:9042 cassandra:3.11
java -jar scalardb-schema-loader-3.5.0.jar --config database.properties --coordinator -f emoney-schema.json
```

### Deploy `kube-prometheus-stack` to the `monitoring` namespace

Deploy `kube-prometheus-stack` by following the step 2 and 3 of the Getting Started with Helm Charts:
https://github.com/scalar-labs/helm-charts/blob/main/docs/getting-started-monitoring.md#step-2-prepare-a-custom-values-file

### Load the latest scalardb-graphql build to minikube

```console
minikube image load ghcr.io/scalar-labs/scalardb-graphql:4.0.0-SNAPSHOT
minikube image tag ghcr.io/scalar-labs/scalardb-graphql:4.0.0-SNAPSHOT local/test/scalardb-graphql:4.0.0-SNAPSHOT
```

### Create a custom values file

```yaml
scalarDbGraphQlConfiguration:
  contactPoints: cassandra-scalardb
  contactPort: 9042
  username: cassandra
  password: cassandra
  storage: cassandra
  logLevel: INFO
  path: /graphql
  namespaces: emoney
  graphiql: "true"

image:
  repository: local/test/scalardb-graphql
  tag: 4.0.0-SNAPSHOT

service:
  type: LoadBalancer

serviceMonitor:
  enabled: true

prometheusRule:
  enabled: true

grafanaDashboard:
  enabled: true

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: nginx
```

### Install scalardb-graphql chart

```console
helm install scalardb-graphql ./charts/scalardb-graphql -f custom-values.yaml
```

### Open Grafana

Run `minikube tunnel` and open http://localhost:3000/.

To cause a GraphQL error, for example, send an invalid GraphQL document like the following:

```console
curl -v http://localhost:8080/graphql -H 'Content-Type: application/graphql' --data '{}'
```

To cause an HTTP error, for example, send a request with an invalid `Content-Type`

```console
curl -v http://localhost:8080/graphql -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' -X POST
```

author: jeasinema
body:
Hi,

Thanks for making this learning list and indeed I learned a lot. Just want to share one of our recent works on transformers and I hope it could help the community through your platform:

RelViT: Concept-guided Vision Transformer for Visual Relational Reasoning (ICLR 2022)
[arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11167) | [code](https://github.com/NVlabs/RelViT)
In this work, we propose a better training scheme for vision transformers and testify it on many visual relational reasoning tasks, including HICO and GQA. We further introduce concept-guided contrastive learning that helps these models master visual reasoning without massive pertaining or extra training data.

author: blaine
body:
This is extremely basic, but shows at least in theory how low-level API access can be managed. Call `handle.getObjId` like:

`handle.getObjId('_root', 'message')` to get the object id of the "message" attribute off the root of the document. That object id can then be used in subsequent calls to various low-level wasm API calls.

n.b. that "mark" is not working because it claims that offsets that are not out of bounds are out of bounds. Not sure what that's about - @orionz?

author: easbar
body:
So far we use the config file to create the encoding manager, whether we run a new import or load an existing graph. This means we have to use the exact same configuration when loading a graph that we used for the import, even though we cannot change the encoding manager after the first import anyway. A more comfortable approach would be loading the encoding manager from the stored data and not having to use the same configuration again.

Another problem with the current approach is that we'd like to store the maximum speeds used during the import so we can use them for the A* heuristics later. So far these values were taken from the config (or the hard-coded defaults). We can store the max values in the encoded values and write them to the properties file (or elsewhere), but then of course we need to read them later when loading the graph. 

Starting with this PR all encoded values, flag encoders (and the encoding manager) are created from a string representation in the properties file when we load the graph. This allows storing the maximum speeds/values along with the encoded value properties.

author: rgommers
body:
This was giving a lot of warnings like:

    numpy/f2py/src/fortranobject.h:9: warning: "NPY_NO_DEPRECATED_API" redefined

when building SciPy. In general, this is generated code which is included in the build of other projects which may have already set this macro - so only set it if it is not yet set.

The other change is to set it to the current numpy version, like is done everywhere else in numpy, rather than to a fixed 1.7 version. This will ensure that if new deprecations happen, f2py gets updated for them.

This came in with gh-19388 recently (not present in the 1.23.x branch).

author: slowbackspace
body:
Hi! We've found a bug affecting **remembered** cardano accounts where rewards earned from staking are not updated if the user doesn't trigger account sync by some other action (eg. by sending or receiving a transaction).

Due to this the withdrawal could fail as the withdrawing amount would not match the total available rewards on the blockchain (partial withdrawals are not possible). 

This PR fixes the condition for detecting outdated cardano account by including a check for a mismatch between account's rewards amount reported by backend and the amount cached in Suite (and also fixes the condition by replacing AND with OR).

author: thallgren
body:
## Description

Prior to this change, the client would forget its session-id when it
was forcefully disconnected and reconnecting to the traffic-manager
would create a new session. As a result, the old session was lost and
all intercepts belonging to it was unavailable. The traffic-manager
would however keep the session alive for 24 hours, and during that time
the intercepts would remain active. An active tcp intercept effectively
blocks all other intercepts to the same workload.

This commit stores the session-id in the client's cache and removes it
only after a successful `Depart`. If the session-id is found in the

attempted call to `Remain`. If the call succeeds, the client will reuse the

body:
### IronCurtain effect on organics
- In vanilla game, when iron-curtain is applied on organic units like infantries and squids, they can only get directly killed by C4Warhead. The effect can now be chosen among
  - `kill` : IronCurtain kills the organic object with a specifc warhead.
  - `invulnerable` : IronCurtain makes the organic object invulnerable like buildings and vehicles.
  - `ignore` : IronCurtain gives no effect on the organic object.

In `rulesmd.ini`
```ini
[CombatDamage]
IronCurtain.EffectOnOrganics=kill  ; IronCurtain effect Enumeration (kill | invulnerable | ignore), IronCurtain to Infantry and Techno with Organic=yes
IronCurtain.KillOrganicsWarhead=   ; IronCurtain uses this warhead to kill organics, default to [CombatDamage]->C4Warhead
[SOMETECHNO]                       ; InfantryType or Organic TechnoType
IronCurtain.Effect=                ; IronCurtain effect Enumeration (kill | invulnerable | ignore), default to [CombatDamage]-> IronCurtain.EffectOnOrganics
IronCurtain.KillWarhead=           ; IronCurtain uses this warhead to kill this organic, default to [CombatDamage]->IronCurtain.KillWarhead
```

author: eshrh
body:
1. Better messages
 I didn't like how for a single key overwrite, there are two errors, one for the key conflict and another for the command redefinition. These really have the same cause. I've combined the two-part message into one and rewrote them slightly for concision and clarity.

2. Option to suppress
Currently, warning messages are sent when redefining keys in your user config. I don't think these are very useful because the user must have explicitly done so. This patch introduces the option `should_warn_about_user_key_override` which when set to 0, only warns the user when they redefine keys within the same file.

*I set this option to 0 by default, so this change would be affecting defaults*.

3. Fixes multiple redefinition issue
When a key is redefined multiple times, the warning message for subsequent redefinitions will still point to the first definitions source file and line. The last commit on this pull request fixes this issue by updating file paths and line numbers when a key is redefined.

This PR allows playing/previewing an audio attachment from the Message Input. A user can play and pause as well as watch the duration, and drag the progress of the audio to a particular location.

When a file of type audio is added we allow playing the audio from the file upload preview. By default, a user can download the file if the package `react-native-video`/`expo-av` isn't available. One of the series of steps to split source files from backends, this PR addresses OpenGL:

- Move OpenGL runtime files to `taichi/runtime/opengl` for target `opengl_runtime`.
- Move OpenGL program impl files to `taichi/runtime/program_impls/opengl` for target `opengl_program_impl`.

The dependency relation is:
`opengl_rhi` <- `opengl_runtime` <- `opengl_program_impl` <- `core`

author: michalstrehovsky
body:
There is an invalid (with hindsight) dataflow warning suppression in System.Linq.Expressions that assumes we'll always have an invocable method body for delegate Invoke method. We need one in IL. We don't in native code.

Emulate what IL Linker does and generate a method body. This is a size regression.

Invalid suppression: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3b2883b097a773715ca84056885e0ca1488da36e/src/libraries/System.Linq.Expressions/src/System/Dynamic/Utils/TypeUtils.cs#L906-L912

Fixes #70880.

Cc @dotnet/ilc-contrib

author: sprenger120
body:
This PR fixes two things that I've found not working at all.   

- First, a statically sized array, while being shown correctly in the UI, always contained zeroes when the service was called. This was due to missing handling of array slot_types which in turn required generation of the correct expression names. 
- Second, filling in a dynamically sized array was not possible (afaik), and always resulted in exceptions thrown in the serialization process due to Python's dicts not supporting access by dot (.), by default. 

I've added a small class called Map, which implements access by dot. This class was not written by be, but rather taken from the supplied stackoverflow link, tell me, if that would be a licensing problem.

To easily test my changes, I've written up a small test application which provides a service with arrays and outputs its content upon being called. See [--> here](https://github.com/sprenger120/array_service_caller_test)

**Potential problem**
A dynamically sized array would be written, for the UI, like this `[{'data1': 1, 'data2': 2}, {'data1': 5, 'data2': 6}]`. If you forget to specify one dict key, present in the message definition, you get the previously mentioned serialization exception again. There needs to be some sort of default initialization of all message members in the dict, but I'm unsure how do it.

author: yinpeiqi
body:
## Description
<!-- Brief description. Refer to the related issues if existed.
It'll be great if relevant reviewers can be assigned as well.-->
This is the limited edge dataloader. (For automatic inference helper).
For the normal node dataloader, the memory consumption of each batch is unbalance. We only fixed the number of target nodes in a batch, while the number of edges are different among different batches. Since we may encounter the cases that many high degree nodes in the same batch, and it become the bottleneck of training/inference. We develop a limited edge dataloader, which user first define two configures: `max_node` and `max_edge`. These two parameters define the maximum number of nodes and the maximum number of edges in the same batch. This dataloader mainly consider the workload of GNN inference.

The limited edge dataloader also support modify `max_node` and `max_edge` during training/inference. (The support for automatic inference).

Here we display an example of using the LimitedEdgeDataloader:
```python
import torch
import dgl
from dgl.dataloading.limited_edge import LimitedEdgeDataloader
from dgl.data import RedditDataset

if __name__ == '__main__':
    data = RedditDataset(self_loop=True)
    g = data[0].to("cuda")
    nids = torch.arange(g.number_of_nodes()).to(g.device)
    sampler = dgl.dataloading.MultiLayerFullNeighborSampler(1)

author: timdirks
body:
Fix bug where the isolated mention character check could return wrong result.

Consider these settings:
```js
{
    allowChars: /^[a-zA-Z0-9.]+$/,
    maxChars: 8,
    isolateCharacter: true,
}
```

If the quill text was `tim@owow.i`. The `getTextBeforeCursor` method would return the last 8 characters before the cursor, which would be `m@owow.i`. The `hasValidMentionCharIndex` would get the `@` index (which is 1) and check if it was isolated (which it isn't). All good and well.

Now I type an extra letter so the quill text becomes `tim@owow.io`, the last 8 characters would now be `@owow.io`. The `hasValidMentionCharIndex` would get the `@` index (which is now 0) and return `true` meaning it thinks it's an isolated mention whilst the bigger scope shows it is not isolated.

My fix gets the one character before the `getTextBeforeCursor` string (if there is anything before it) and passes it to the `hasValidMentionCharIndex` function. Now the function checks IF the `@` index is 0, the one character mention character prefix is either an empty string (meaning the text range is the beginning of the Quill) or is a whitespace character. Both cases mean the mention character is isolated. If neither cases are true, the character is not isolated.

author: jamikettunen
body:
#### Testing the changes
- I tested the changes in this PR: **briefly**

This significantly speeds up the package building process for build scripts etc. that run `./xbps-src pkg ...` on a long list of packages that may already have up-to-date local packages built when configured with `XBPS_PRESERVE_PKGS` set.

~~I still have one question: what to do with the existing call to `check_existing_pkg` in [`common/xbps-src/libexec/build.sh`](https://github.com/void-linux/void-packages/blob/master/common/xbps-src/libexec/build.sh#L38)? The script appears to be executed from a [few](https://github.com/void-linux/void-packages/tree/master/common/xbps-src/shutils/cross.sh) [other](https://github.com/void-linux/void-packages/tree/master/common/xbps-src/shutils/build_dependencies.sh) [scripts](https://github.com/void-linux/void-packages/tree/master/common/xbps-src/shutils/bulk.sh) as well so I left it alone for now.~~

#### Example with a single package
Before this patch:
```
void-packages $ time ./xbps-src pkg helvum
=> xbps-src: updating repositories for host (x86_64)...
[*] Updating repository `https://repo-default.voidlinux.org/current/x86_64-repodata' ...
[*] Updating repository `https://repo-default.voidlinux.org/current/nonfree/x86_64-repodata' ...
[*] Updating repository `https://repo-default.voidlinux.org/current/debug/x86_64-repodata' ...
[*] Updating repository `https://repo-default.voidlinux.org/current/multilib/x86_64-repodata' ...
[*] Updating repository `https://repo-default.voidlinux.org/current/multilib/nonfree/x86_64-repodata' ...
=> xbps-src: updating software in / masterdir...
=> xbps-src: cleaning up / masterdir...
=> helvum-0.3.4_2: removing autodeps, please wait...
=> WARNING: helvum-0.3.4_2: skipping build due to existing /host/binpkgs//helvum-0.3.4_2.x86_64.xbps

real	0m1.980s
user	0m0.504s
sys	0m0.113s
```
After this patch:
```
void-packages $ time ./xbps-src pkg helvum
=> WARNING: helvum-0.3.4_2: skipping build due to existing /host/binpkgs//helvum-0.3.4_2.x86_64.xbps

real	0m0.062s
user	0m0.041s
sys	0m0.024s
```
Previously this would add up to about a minute of waiting for essentially no reason if 30 packages already have up-to-date local packages, while with this patch it would only take about 2 seconds to come to the same conclusion with the same package list.

author: ndp-opendap
body:
Replaced usage of the `std::vector` access pattern `&v[0]` with the c++11 method `std::vector::.data()` in the hope that this change will address rh8 SIGABRT issues that seemed tied to the old pattern.

The c++11 access method `std::vector::data()` is discussed here:

- https://cplusplus.com/reference/vector/vector/data/

This PR is an experiment to see if James' assertion that the implementation of `std::vector` may have changed in RH8 could be at the root of the zero-length array SIGABRT problems.  When I saw that the class had this "new" c++11 method I figured it would be worth a shot to see if this would address the issue.

If this does produce a fix I think we will want to write a ticket to make a similar refactor throughout both the libdap code and BES code. Once bitten, etc.

A quick search of *.cc and *.h files in **`libdap4`** and **`bes`** for things matching **`&[a-zA-Z0-9]+\[0\]`** shows ~1100 occurrences of the access pattern that we may need to address.

author: pinkforest
body:
Addresses #405 
- openssl-src 111 release stream is not supposed to be affected by this advisory
- openssl-src has two release streams - 111 for 1.1.1 and 300 for 3.0 vendored OpenSSL
- openssl-src release stream 111 brings vendored openssl 1.1.1 and
- openssl-src release stream 300 brings vendored openssl 3.0
- I've fixed the advisory to make sure only 300 release stream is advised to upgrade as 111 is unaffected
- This is pinging a lot of people as this widely used vendored openssl uses 111 release stream

author: lewtun
body:
This PR does two main things:

* It pins the list of supported metrics to what is currently supported as of today. The `get_supported_metrics()` function relies on having _all_ metric Python dependencies in the same environment, and is very slow. Instead I did a single run offline and added the result in the application itself. We can revisit dynamically listing the supported metrics if https://github.com/huggingface/evaluate/issues/138 becomes available
* Moves the metric info box to the help button to declutter the UI. I've also clarified what is meant by "default arguments"

author: russellseymour
body:
## 📲 What

Added a new task in the pipeline called `setup:environment` which calls the `Confirm-Environment` PowerShell function to ensure all the enviornment variables exist for the successful running of the pipeline

## 🤔 Why

After the last PR the release stage ran but there was no release on GitHub.

By adding the `Confirm-Environment` is it possible now to check that all the required enviornment variables exist to allow the task to complete.

## 🛠 How

Modified the `context.yaml` file so that the module itself is picked up, this means that the latest version is being used when performing the build.

Added  a new file `stage_envvars.yml` to the repo to ensure that the `Confirm-Enviornment` function has the necessary config to determine which vars should exist.

## 👀 Evidence

When the guard for running a release on a branch was removed a release was created on GitHub. This release has been removed.

Notes for QA

## Description

This PR simply adds the option to perform automatically an energy minimization for each end state. Here the idea is to follow the same principle as for the "optimized state generation" where the energy offset is chosen to offset the system into one particular state. This allows to remove any contacts between that specific state and the protein/solvent which leads to early SHAKE errors.

howonlee
body: Pursuant to #21695. Root cause is that it indeed doesn't look for the DB-level data perm access enablement when looking at a native query's permissions. Fix entails getting it to look for that one specific perm, basically. A note of worry comes into mind, because we actually have no guarantee that just-running a native query doesn't mutate anything. Indeed, worst case I could think of is that the native query executes a sproc when you even just see the card or something like that, there's certainly nothing preventing that on the MB side. On the other hand, such a mutation-causing query would be a pretty strange thing to shove into a BI query editor. Do we just consider that user error or warn about the possibility in that case? Finding mutating SQL queries seems infeasible for an MB-side fix. - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/metabase/metabase/23407)

## Description of the new Feature/Bugfix
1. Kerning and ligatures can be enabled for LayoutProcessor by calling LayoutProcessor.enableKernLiga();

Shows all letters and sequences of DIN 91379 in a new

[GlyphLayoutDocumentDin91379.pdf](https://github.com/LibrePDF/OpenPDF/files/9578488/GlyphLayoutDocumentDin91379.pdf)

PDF-form.
[GlyphLayoutFormDin91379.pdf](https://github.com/LibrePDF/OpenPDF/files/9578485/GlyphLayoutFormDin91379.pdf)

### GlyphLayoutDocumentKernLiga.java
Enables LayoutProcessor with kerning and ligatures for all fonts
[GlyphLayoutDocumentKernLiga.pdf](https://github.com/LibrePDF/OpenPDF/files/9578487/GlyphLayoutDocumentKernLiga.pdf)

### GlyphLayoutDocumentKernLigaPerFont.java
Enables LayoutProcessor with kerning and/or ligatures for specified fonts
[GlyphLayoutDocumentKernLigaPerFont.pdf](https://github.com/LibrePDF/OpenPDF/files/9578486/GlyphLayoutDocumentKernLigaPerFont.pdf)

### GlyphLayoutDocumentBidi.java
Prints bidirectional text with correct glyph layout, kerning and ligatures globally enabled
[GlyphLayoutDocumentBidi.pdf](https://github.com/LibrePDF/OpenPDF/files/9578490/GlyphLayoutDocumentBidi.pdf)

### GlyphLayoutDocumentBidiPerFont.java
Prints bidirectional text with correct glyph layout, kerning and ligatures globally enabled. Direction can be chosen per font
[GlyphLayoutDocumentBidiPerFont.pdf](https://github.com/LibrePDF/OpenPDF/files/9578489/GlyphLayoutDocumentBidiPerFont.pdf)




## Compatibilities Issues
New methods added, existing methods in LayoutProcessor are unchanged.

body:
The `RustFmtRange` command should not attempt to reformat any child modules of the module currently being formatted.

Without this change, I get the following error when attempting to format a range:
```
rust.vim: was not able to parse rustfmt messages. Here is the raw output:

Error writing files: failed to resolve mod `foo`: /private/var/folders/lx/810r91ls7nz_mf24vhv_94w40000gp/T/vWfCEK6/dy
foo.rs does not exist
Error detected while processing function rustfmt#FormatRange[4]..<SNR>92_RunRustfmt:
line  104:
E776: No location list
```

While `--skip-children` is unstable, the `--file-lines` option itself is also unstable, so this seems like it shouldn't be an issue.

The client certificate used by Ondat must be in the same namespace as Ondat, hence the default must be 'storageos'

This error didn't surface much because the etcd operator creates the secret in the right place. But if a customer has been using an external Etcd and creating a Secret with their TLS material, the command would be wrong. Before, the CR had the option to specify what NS the secret could be found, but that is no longer the case.

author: semd
body:
## Summary

We have found a bug in the Home page for the Security Solution plugin, caused by the solution being filtered using the `navLinks`. The Security link panel was not appearing, in a random manner.

### Bug Explanation

Recently we did a change in the Security Solution plugin to lazy-load all the `deepLinks` configs, since they were growing too much, so we changed the plugin initialization with empty `deepLinks`, and used the `updater$` to set them on during the plugin `start`. 
Also, the plugin "root" needs to be _hidden_, as we only want to show internal links in the global navigation and global search. 

On the other hand, the Home page plugin, to render the solution panels takes the registered solutions and filters them checking that they have at least one visible link, which is good. The problem is that Security doesn't have any visible link until the `deepLinks` are loaded and updated, which happens asynchronously.

So when the Home page renders, the Security panel appears randomly, depending on the `deepLinks` being updated before or after the Home renders.

![home_bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17747913/174328028-4c726684-d6d5-421b-8177-40709502c259.png)

### Bug Fix

We have implemented [a small patch on our side](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/134577/commits/bea8a0181dd33f5a491a87b63c3d0d003d7a63c2) to prevent that, by initializing the Security plugin root as _visible_, and when the `deepLinks` are updated we also change the app status back to _hidden_, this way the Home page always finds some visible link.

Even though, we think that this is not ideal, we had to come to the Home page to understand what was going on, and we had to initialize the app in an unwanted temporary state to prevent it. And the same problem may also happen to other Solutions in the future.

We have put together this small fix on the Home plugin side, that takes advantage of the `navLinks` being observable, so the Home page solutions can be updated when the `navLinks` changes. This way the Security panel will always be displayed, regardless of the plugin being initialized as _hidden_.

![home_fix](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17747913/174336376-53a93047-ef81-4590-a5fd-9f1424765c44.png)

body: Added support for compiler arguments to g++ within the cell magic declaration. Any arguments after "--" will be passed as arguments to g++, and anything before will be passed as arguments to the cpp magic. For example, you can use "%%cpp -t -- -O3 -lpthread" at the beginning of your cell. This will run "timeit" on the cpp magic, while passing the "-O3" and "-lpthread" arguments to g++.

author: adcroft
body:
- The PGI compiler was complaining about some `intent(in) :: CS` in MOM_restart.F90. This was because of a line that changes the state of data pointed to from within `CS`, but not `CS` itself: `CS%restart_field(n)%initialized = .true.`.  The strict interpretation is that `CS` is not modified because `CS%restart_field` is a pointer to memory elsewhere. However, the `intent(in)` indicates to the user/programmer that nothing changes and since all arguments to the functions are `intent(in)` most entities, including the PGI compiler, should be surprised that something changed as a result of a passive "query" function. This strict interpretation allows a devious(?) hidden-change-of-state to occur.
- Changing the intent to `intent(inout)` has the consequence that the new intent has to be propagated upwards through the code. And why should a type be `intent(out)` for query functions?
- This commit removes the offending lines that change the state. Apparently we didn't need them!

**Steps to prep SES to test this PR:**

1. Go to SES console for $AWS_REGION and create a new origin and destination emails. AWS will send a verification via email which you'll need to complete. 
2. Find and replace instances in the repo of "testsender", "testreceiver" and "dispostable.com", with the origin and destination email address you verified in step 1 above. 

TODO: environmentally variable-ize these origin and destination email address vals and modify migrations as necessary

**Steps to prep SNS:**

1. Go to Pinpoints console for $AWS_PINPOINT_REGION and choose "create new project", then "configure for sms"
2. Tick the box at the top to enable SMS, choose "transactional" as the default type and save
3. In the lefthand sidebar, go the "SMS and Voice" (bottom) and choose "Phone Numbers"
4. Under "Number Settings" choose "Request Phone Number" 
5. Choose Toll-free number, tick SMS, untick Voice, choose "transactional", hit next and then "request"
6. Go to SNS console for $AWS_PINPOINT_REGION, look at lefthand sidebar under "Mobile" and go to "Text Messaging (SMS)" 
7. Scroll down to "Sandbox destination phone numbers" and tap "Add phone number" then follow the steps to verify (you'll need to be able to retrieve a code sent to each number)

At this point, you _should_ be able to complete both the email and phone verification steps of the Notify user sign up process! 🎉

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a `fission generate credentials` command to create Ed25519 key pairs and their associated DIDs.

This PR fixes/implements the following **bugs/features**

* [x] Add `fission generate credentials` command

The credentials subcommand has no options and only generates Ed25519 key pairs

```
»  ~/.local/bin/fission generate credentials --help
Usage: fission generate credentials 
  Generate an Ed25519 key pair and an associated DID

Available options:
  -h,--help                Show this help text
```

The output prints a private key, public key, and DID

```
»  ~/.local/bin/fission generate credentials
✅ Generated an Ed25519 key pair and associated DID
🗝️  Private key: <private-key>
🔑 Public key: <public-key>
🆔 DID: <DID>
```

This PR also adds a top-level `generate` command with no fallbacks. It must be used with the `credentials` subcommand. The description for the `generate` command in `fission --help` is "Generate key pairs and DIDs".


## Test plan (required)

Compile, then run the `fission credentials generate` command to generate a test key pair and DID.

Check the help text for `fission`, `fission generate` and `fission generate credentials`.

## Closing issues

Closes #613

author: edbertchan
body:
This change allows us to control individual actions via their mneonics. We notice that in large codebases, the volatility of estimates is extremely high for post-build operations such as dexing.

**Why do we not put the estimate directly in the action itself? Why do we need to override it in resource manager?**

If you look up the usage of .setMneonic(), you will see that they all exist in packages and classes and not every class has access to the options.

It seems very complicated to give every place that spawnActionBuilder gets created and used access to the override options. The fix becomes simpler when we call it before resourceManager gets invoked.

You are also not guaranteed where/when resoucebuilder gets called in the future. This can cause additional breakage in the option if the developer forgets to write it there.

**Other Issues/Request For Feedback**

I am not sure about sticking a parsing operation inside of ResourceManager like I currently am. This seems extremely odd. But options itself does not have exposure to ResourceSet.


This is to fufill feature request: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/15668

Sample usage:
build:devpod --mnemonic_resource_override=KotlinFoldJarsAbi=2200,4

## Why are these changes needed?

<!-- Please give a short summary of the change and the problem this solves. -->

`test_serve_head.py`'s `ray_start_stop()` fixture uses the Ray CLI to start and stop Ray between tests. However, sometimes Ray is already started before the test suite begins ([ex. 1](https://buildkite.com/ray-project/ray-builders-branch/builds/8210#01816f71-fcb8-4067-a29a-194b7700b301/1577-2647), [ex. 2](https://buildkite.com/ray-project/ray-builders-pr/builds/35820#01816e16-200a-4b24-9286-f74d0f8afd5c/3104-4173)– thanks @architkulkarni for finding these!). This causes the test to timeout since the fixture fails.

This change stops Ray using the CLI _before_ any of the unit tests start in order to prevent any state sharing.

###### Description of changes

This PR adds `polaris`, its sub-dependency `polaris-web`, and a nixos module to run it.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/140964/174354226-04e7422f-8dc5-43e1-a4dc-3c05e873e9a3.png)

Polaris is a self-hosted music streaming server, with a web and android frontend. The web frontend is included in the official releases.
https://github.com/agersant/polaris

`polaris-web` lies in a separate github repository, and inspired by the packages `jellyfin` and `jellyfin-web` I chose to build `polaris-web` as a separate package.
`polaris-web` uses an odd versioning schema upstream: "build-X". I chose to reuse these tags. Official `polaris` releases (Github actions CI) automatically fetches and bundles the latest available version of `polaris-web`, however `polaris` has seen no new release since april 2021, while `polaris-web` has since had 5 version bumps. Currently I package the version of 'polaris-web' which is being bundled with the current `polaris` release on Github. Once I have properly tested the newer versions I might upgrade.

body:
### Amostrador

Um dos requisitos é mostrar o funcionamento do MLP com **apenas treinamento** e com **treinamento e validação**.

Para isso durante a aula a professora sugeriu a utilização do `holdout` e mostrou a lógica do `k-fold-cross-validation`, para verificar quando há `over-fit` do modelo

### Lógica

Para manter a compatibilidade com o que já fomos fazendo, criei uma classe `GeradorDeAmostras` que tem 2 métodos:
- `holdout` 
- `k_fold`

Ambos métodos retornam uma classe `Amostra` que tem o atributo `folds`, cada fold é composto de um par `treinamento` e validação.

### Qual Utilizar ?

Sinceramente, dado que o modelo não está com `over-fit` acho que faz mais sentido utilizarmos o `holdout` por ser mais rápido de executar e terá o mesmo resultado do treinamento com 3 folds.

### Utilização

Ainda não refatorei, mas no método `treina` do MLP temos que separar o processamento da época em treinamento e validação 


### Arquivos

Criei um arquivo `testa-gerenciador-de-amostras` que pode ser removido, mas que exemplifica a sua utilização:

```py
gerenciador = GerenciadorArquivos("dados/caracteres-limpo.csv")
amostrador = GeradorDeAmostras()

base_caracteres = gerenciador.le_csv(df_caracteres=True, salvar=False)
X_caracteres, y_caracteres = gerenciador.extrai_X_y(base_caracteres, True)


amostra_holdout = amostrador.holdout(X_caracteres, y_caracteres)

treinamento, validacao = amostra_holdout.obter_fold(0)

# Mostra 14 como resultado, ou seja 14 X_caracteres para treinamento
print(len(treinamento[0]))

# Mostra 7 como resultado, ou seja 7 X_caracteres para validação
print(len(validacao[0]))
```

### Notebook

No arquivo `testa-gerenciador-de-amostras` ele está escrevendo 2 arquivos:
- `valida-holdout.csv`
- `valida-kfold.csv`

Para verificar se o processo ocorreu corretamente, é só arrastar esses arquivos para `notebook/data` e eu criei uma página chamada `visualizar-dataset` onde você passa o caminho do arquivo e ele renderiza as letras

### Refatorações

Eu não utilizei muito de `list-comprehensions` e afins, se achar que tem maneira de deixar melhor :)

author: luizstacio
body:
After we insert the `gas_price_factor` to calculate gas, the `verify_gas` started to break, because it didn't consider the  `gas_price_factor` when calculating the `gas.checked_sub(total_gas_required)` causing the TX to not pass the validation.

On this fix I made:
- Change the retrieve `gas` available amount to also filter by `AssetId:default()` as outputs do.
- Calculate the `total_gas_required` and divide it by the `gas_price_factor` and `ceil` the result.

Now when returning the error `InsufficientFeeAmount` it would present the two values in the final amount as ex.: `{ provided: 1, required: 2 }`.

Use case:
In a wallet with 1000000 `Native Coins`
I'm going to do a TX that consumes ~2000000 Gas Units which cost in native coins `(<Gas Units>/<Gas Price Factor>) = 2 Native Coins`
When sending the TX it was failing with the return `InsufficientFeeAmount { provided: 1000000, required: 1999992 }`
Wich is incorrect because the `required fee` should be `1999992/1000000 = 2 Native Coins`.

Notes:
If I add an amount of 3000000 `Native Coins` to the wallet, it would work and consume just the correct amount ~2 Native Coins.

author: peterldowns
body:
Hi, we here at Pipe have been huge fans of sqlboiler for years now and I am excited to be able to (hopefully) contribute something back. We've noticed that generating models has grown extremely slow for us -- it takes about a minute to generate around 190 different `<model>.go` files. We re-generate models quite frequently while developing, which means that this has been a particular pain point for us. I finally got around to doing some performance investigation, and found that we could speed things up so that it would only take about 5 seconds!

This PR speeds the psql/postgres driver up by moving the uniqueness query (used to determine if a given column is unique) from happening once-per-table-per-run to happening once-per-run, and caching the results on the driver.

Unlike previously, the code will query for the uniqueness status of _all_ columns across _all_ tables across _all_ schemas, not just the ones that are being generated. I don't expect this to cause any issues but if this is a barrier to merging it, it shouldn't be too hard to change it to only query against specific schemas/tables.

Based on testing locally, I believe this is the most significant possible speedup for the postgres driver. Some other small improvements that I tried that were effective, but not so dramatically:
* Running the `Columns()` method in parallel for multiple tables at once (observed change: 60 seconds -> 40 seconds)
  * Also increasing the max open / max idle connections on the connection used by the driver
* Fixing `o(n^2)` behavior in column/table reference comparisons (observed change: 40 seconds -> 35 seconds)
  * There are a lot of places where lists are iterated over and over again, which could ~simply be replaced by a map
* Other sql query changes to avoid re-querying column information multiple times (not tested, but given how much this query change improved things, I would expect there to be other wins available)

author: darrensiegel
body:
This PR addresses a collection of issues related to the "Insights" view and the underlying analytics, including:

1. Allow analytics to pick up results from material that has been "remixed" into a course section, as opposed to content that exists because it came in within the "base project".  The solution here was to track the `project_id` in each generated snapshot, pulling it from the `section resource`.  Prior to this the analytics queries were relying on identifying snapshots via the attached section's `base_project_id`
2. Fix the counting of number of attempts in the objective query.  This was incorrect in cases where more than one objective was attached to a part.  
3. Proper handling of objective attachment "at the time of the attempt". Currently the queries consider an attempt to target an objective if any attempt for the same activity was for a revision of the activity that targeted an objective. The fix here was to count the distinct `part_attempt_id` instead of just the number of records. 
4. Moved the filtering and sorting of the Insights view out of rendering. 
5. Lowered the system impact of the Insights view by making the "By Page" and "By Objective" queries execute on demand, when the user first clicks those buttons to view them.  The button itself will display a spinning loading indicator until the query finishes and the table displays. 
6. Renders the "By Objective" results in a way that preserves and expresses the "parent - child" relationship of LOs and sub-LOs
7. Fixes sorting, which was just simply not working because it was using string based keys to extract the sort field when it needed to use the Atom equivalent. 

Closes #2693

author: twstokes
body:
Fixes #17719

Ref: p4a5px-2Pl-p2

## Description

There appears to be a race where:
1. The table view is initialized with the number of existing objects in Core Data.
2. [Core Data is wiped](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-iOS/blob/779d17b297caba127853df1a290a88c9039a8e60/WordPress/Classes/ViewRelated/People/PeopleViewController.swift#L176).
3. As the table view renders its cells it tries to access objects that no longer exist.

This PR adds two safeguards:
1. Until `isInitialLoad` is cleared, don't render any cells if asked.
2. If trying to render a cell using an invalid index path, return a hidden cell.

With item 1 in place I'm doubtful item 2 will occur, but it's there to be extra safe.

## Note

Interestingly I could _not_ reproduce the crash, even without these fixes, when running from the 20.1 release branch.

## Crash reproduction

To see if your device is susceptible to crashing, load WordPress 20.0.1 from the App Store and follow the testing steps expecting a crash at step 7. I've only been able to reproduce it using an iPad Pro.

### Video of crash:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2092798/174352365-bc5a9d0f-96c6-40b4-8f71-b2e0de74c5dc.mp4

## Testing

All testing can be done on a .com Simple site. 

**Prerequisites:**
- iPad Pro with WPiOS in full screen
- A site with at least two Users added (a User has the role of Administrator, Editor, Author, or Contributor)
- **Important:** Only the alpha and release builds seem to crash (presumably due to faster execution). A debug build running in Simulator or on a physical device will probably not crash. [Use the alpha build from this PR](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-iOS/pull/18907#issuecomment-1159210291).

**Steps:**
1. Load WPiOS in full screen mode
2. Tap People
3. Observe that the users for the site load (there should be at least two, see prerequisites)
4. Tap another view such (e.g. Sharing, Menus, Themes)
5. Tap People
6. Repeat steps 5 and 6
7. Expect no crashes

## Regression Notes
1. Potential unintended areas of impact
    - Regressions to the People view - managing users, syncing changes.

2. What I did to test those areas of impact (or what existing automated tests I relied on)
    - Manual testing on iPad and iPhone.

3. What automated tests I added (or what prevented me from doing so)
    - None. We should consider moving to an approach in the future where the view is decoupled from the data syncing.

PR submission checklist:

- [x] I have completed the Regression Notes.
- [x] I have considered adding unit tests for my changes.
- [x] I have considered adding accessibility improvements for my changes.
- [x] I have considered if this change warrants user-facing release notes and have added them to `RELEASE-NOTES.txt` if necessary.

author: jsha
body:
Expanding `$@` means that if a positional parameter has an internal
space, e.g. "foo bar", it will be split into two positional parameters
in the resulting command, e.g. "foo" "bar". Expanding `"$@"` ensures
that such parameters are quoted during expansion, so we still get
"foo bar" in the exec command, which is always what we wanted.

author: timwoj
body:
This is something I've had sitting on a branch and have been rebasing for over a year now. I had intended to do more to it before doing a PR, but instead decided to take one leap and get this part in first. The rest can come later, and is described below. This isn't ready for merging yet, since it depends on a couple of commits in the deprecation-removal work that I'll open a PR for after 5.0 is officially out. Only the "Convert" commit below is core to this work.

This PR converts the `Dictionary`, `DictIterator`, `RobustDictIterator`, and `DictEntry` types to be templates. This has the fortunate side effect of removing the need to store the value in each entry as a `void*`, since we can now know the actual type stored in the dictionary. The only changes outside of the Dict files are the need to remove uses of `DictEntry::GetValue<>` (now a deprecated method) and the need to specify template types for iterators. My only real concern with these changes is the potential for a bit slower build times, since most of the code was moved out of `Dict.cc` and into `Dict.h`, which means the whole thing needs to be read every time we include it (which is roughly a third of the build).

Also included is a commit that turns `PDict` into a simple type alias. This requires adding a few more functions to the base `Dictionary` class, but it leaves the possibility to just remove `PDict` altogether (after deprecation) and rely just on the base class for all dictionary objects.

Future things I'd like to tackle:
- Making the outward-facing dictionary API more like `std::map`'s, just like we did for `List` a couple years ago.
- Support [structured bindings](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/structured_binding) for iteration. I started working on this originally and it became quite complicated with the keying stuff in `DictEntry`. I haven't revisited it in a while and I might have a better idea now.
- Better commenting in the `Dict` header for the outward-facing API.

This PR is dependent on some of the deprecation cleanup in https://github.com/zeek/zeek/pull/2199 and that should be merged first.

author: square789
body:
Copypaste of the first commit message follows:
```
- Fix a bug where indices local to a loop instead of the actual block member indices were written to a uniform dict,
  which caused KeyErrors in the creation of the UniformBlock views.
- Shaders are now set up to read each uniform block from the uniform buffer binding point with the same index as the block.
  - This should not affect any existing shaders as none of them use more than one block (the WindowBlock), which is still
    sourced from 0 and whose UBO binds to 0.
  - Shaders do not have their block bindings configured by UniformBufferObjects anymore.
- Views are now created when required for each WindowBlock and not by each UBO when it is created. 
```
I've ran the sprite examples before and after and couldn't tell of any problems there, but this will ruin third-party code using the library if it relied on some of the exotic binding behavior of the UBOs or of their coupling to ShaderPrograms.
If the decoupling of UBOs to a specific ShaderProgram is undesired, feel free to drop the second commit.

author: hawkw
body:
Tower [v0.4.13] includes a fix for a bug in the `tower::ready_cache`
module, tower-rs/tower#415. The `ready_cache` module is used internally
in Tower's load balancer. This bug resulted in panics in the proxy
(linkerd/linkerd2#8666, linkerd/linkerd2#6086) in cases where the
Destination service sends a very large number of service discovery
updates (see linkerd/linkerd2#8677).

This commit updates the proxy's dependency on `tower` to 0.4.13, to
ensure that this bugfix is picked up.

Fixes linkerd/linkerd2#8666
Fixes linkerd/linkerd2#6086

[v0.4.13]: https://github.com/tower-rs/tower/releases/tag/tower-0.4.13

author: sgreiner
body:
mysqli_stmt::bind_param() does not accept unknown named parameters
When $params contains non numeric (named) array keys, PHP 8 will
not pass them positional and tries to map it to named parameters
of mysqli_stmt::bind_param which fails.
https://www.php.net/manual/de/mysqli-stmt.bind-param.php
array_values() will make sure a numeric array is passed. It should
not change the position of the params inside the array.

body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

`EditorPreviewPane` for AsyncAPI now contains its own separate ValidationPane. This new ValidationPane displays the results from the asyncapi/parser, and maintains the error message to user to fix the errors (while not rendering AsyncApi-React). These errors are also stored in Redux state.

The additional benefit is that `EditorPreviewPane` now displays more detailed error messages indicating why AsyncApi-React is unable to render. It is also now visually deterministic which errors breaks AsyncApi-React rendering, e.g. there could be other errors, but do not impact rendering of the AsyncApi definition.

`Jump to Marker` feature also works, matching the behavior of `EditorPane`'s `ValidationPane`, e.g. clicking on the error will cause the pointer to move to the appropriate line in `EditorPane`.


### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
<!--- Use the magic "Fixes #1234" format, so the issues are -->
<!--- automatically closed when this PR is merged. -->

AsyncAPI definitions are first parsed by AsyncApi's own parser. If parsing fails, AsyncApi-React will be unable to render the definition. 
Current issues:
- parsing errors resulting from the `asyncpi/parser` has a different error shape than parsing errors from `apidom-ls`.
- sharing the `ValidationPane` within the `EditorPane` can cause async visual conflicts depending on which parser returns errors "later".
- `apidom-ls` and `asyncapi/parser` can return different errors and different error counts.

author: skye
body:
The TPU tracer, which is necessary for populating TPU events in a
profile, will abort initialization if libtpu isn't initialized:
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/1f4d1e5c832f8a50ea49a1659dec0db01a1fc4d8/tensorflow/core/profiler/backends/tpu/tpu_tracer.cc#L124-L127

This change makes sure all JAX backends are initialized before
creating a profiler trace, which is when the TPU tracer will be
initialized. In particular, we want to make sure that the Cloud TPU
backend is initialized if it's available (if it's not available, the
TPU tracer isn't expected to initialize).

The breakage was initially introduced in
https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/pull/55429 on May 4, but was
only caught via ProfilerTest.testProgrammaticProfilingon in
profiler_test.py starting June 10. We believe something must have
changed in the test or JAX itself to cause this issue to only show up
later. I would ideally figure out how to write a more robust
regression test, but in the interest of fixing TPU profiling, this
change is only tested via the existing profiler tests.

author: cromerc
body:
Added zstd compression support. To show how useful zstd is I am using it on a map I have that has 141x32 tiles. These are the file sizes of that one map with different compressions:
CSV(uncompressed): 47.2kB
Base64(uncompressed): 121.2kB
Base64(gzip): 2.2kB
Base64(zlib): 2.1kB
Base64(zstd): 1.9kB

However one of the biggest factors isn't just the size of the file. zstd is known for being faster at decompressing data than gzip and zlib. Which means that import times in godot for the maps are so much faster, especially for really large maps. This saves a lot of development time each time you have to modify a big map or importing many maps at once.

author: kunalspathak
body:
Currently, the base version for armarch is v8.0. However, starting v8.1, there are faster `atomic` instructions that takes less instructions and do not need full barrier. See example: https://godbolt.org/z/x1o9Ybh66. This restricts the machine that supports the CPU feature from using these faster instructions. As part of this PR, added a flag `g_arm64_atomics_present` that is set at the startup when we get the CPU capability info. Below APIs are rewritten such that it checks this flag and use the faster instructions if atomic support is available on the machine:

- InterlockedCompareExchange
- InterlockedCompareExchangeAcquire
- InterlockedCompareExchangeRelease

Finally, the usage of these APIs at certain hot code paths (mostly in `syncblk.*` files) are replaced with the rewritten APIs.

This does introduce an extra check for the flag, but it is cheaper than any other alternative like function pointer. With function pointer, there has to be an extra call and it has to go through CFG which makes it more expensive.

Clang [added a flag](https://reviews.llvm.org/rG4d7df43ffdb460dddb2877a886f75f45c3fee188) `-moutline-atomics` recently that would emit such check during compilation so the faster machines can take advantage of it while still maintaining compatibility with the older machines. See an example [here](https://mysqlonarm.github.io/ARM-LSE-and-MySQL/). Unfortunately, we are still on clang9 and hopefully, this PR and the improvements I share below will motivate us to move to newer compiler on Linux to have this taken care by compiler. Hence, for now I just introduced this on Windows. The MSVC story on windows is slightly different. It doesn't have an equivalent flag like `-moutline-atomics` so the only option to generate faster atomic instructions would be to use `/arch:armv8.1` as mentioned [here](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/msvc-backend-updates-in-visual-studio-2022-version-17-2/), which unfortunately we cannot do. So the choice was to add such check manually in our codebase to take advantage of the atomic instructions.

## Benchmark
I tested this PR with following C# code:

```c#
namespace Monitor_Lock  
{  
    class Program  
    {  
        static readonly object _object = new object();  
        static long result = 0;
  
        static void TestLock()  
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < 10000; i++)
            {
                lock (_object)  
                {  
                    result += i;
                }
            }
        }  
  
        static void Main(string[] args)      
        {
            Stopwatch sw = new Stopwatch();
            int count = int.Parse(args[0]);
            List<Thread> threads = new List<Thread>();
            sw.Start();
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)  
            {  
                ThreadStart start = new ThreadStart(TestLock);  
                Thread thread = new Thread(start);
                threads.Add(thread);
                thread.Start();
            }
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)
            {
                threads[i].Join();
            }
            sw.Stop();
            Console.WriteLine($"{count} threads took {sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds} msec.");
        }
    }  
}  
```

author: srividya-sundaram
body:
Summary of what this PR does:

Prior to this PR, we had the following 2 warnings for floating-point precision change:

```
-Wimplicit-float-conversion : (example) implicit conversion loses floating-point precision: 'double' to 'float'
-Wdouble-promotion          : (example) implicit conversion increases floating-point precision: 'float' to 'double'
```

Both the above warnings were turned off by default and only enabled when the corresponding warning flags were passed.
Also, both the warnings were only specific to Clang and were not enabled for SYCL (meaning device code).
If the floating point values remained the same on both the source and target semantics after the cast, no warning was emitted.

Example:
```
float PrecisionLoss = 1.1;  // implicit conversion loses floating-point precision: 'double' to 'float'
float SizeChange = 3.0;   // In this case, though we have assigned a double value to a 'float' variable, there is techncally no loss of precision and we don't get any warning here. 
But there is still a change in floating-point-rank (size) here ( from 'double' to 'float')
```
This PR identifies a floating-point size change after an implicit cast and triggers a warning when the -Wimplicit-float-size-conversion flag is passed. It is turned off by default.
This warning is enabled for both Clang and SYCL(i.e both host and device code)
The only other case this addresses is, if there is a precision loss and `-Wimplicit-float-size-conversion` is passed but `-Wimplicit-float-conversion` is not, we make sure to emit at least a size warning.

## PR Summary

<!--Please provide at least 1-2 sentences describing the pull request in
detail.  Why is this change required?  What problem does it solve?-->

<!--If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here.-->

This PR implements prolongation-in-one routines, analogous to the restriction-in-one routines. As with restriction-in-one, the old per meshblock/per face routines now point to the in-one routines to (a) test them and ensure they work and (b) reduce code duplicaiton. 

I made this change for the following reasons:
1. It paves the way to cleanup the boundary value machinery and move entirely to in-one routines as we move forward.
2. It's a useful place to hook in for other prolongation/restriction routines, such as face-centered fields or higher-order methods.
3. (Most immediately) I plan to start modifying physical boundaries to support an in-one kind of code-path.

As of now, no coalescence is actually taking place, so this should have no correctness or performance impact. It's just a forward-looking code cleanup.

body:
<!--
  Please check the needed checkboxes ([ ] -> [x]). Leave the
  comments as they are, they won’t show on GitHub.

  a general description of the changes, and remember, it’s up to you to convince

### Initial checklist

*   [x] I read the support docs <!-- https://github.com/vfile/.github/blob/main/support.md -->
*   [x] I read the contributing guide <!-- https://github.com/vfile/.github/blob/main/contributing.md -->

*   [x] I searched issues and couldn’t find anything (or linked relevant results below) <!-- https://github.com/search?q=user%3Avfile&type=Issues -->
*   [x] If applicable, I’ve added docs and tests

### Description of changes

Last weekend I was working on a freelance job and my team had issues with `vfile` package, since (for some weird reason) Typescript couldn't find all the types available from `vfile` package (e.g.: Data, MaybeBuffer, Value, Options, ReporterSettings, Compatible, DataMap, and BufferEncoding). I quickly forked and rewrote all the files to `.ts` and exported the "missing types" from `vfile` package (the ones the freelance job was throwing errors).

Everything worked fine with my rewrite and we used it until yesterday. The project maintainer decided to remove `vfile` from the project, thus making my rewrites not needed anymore. This is why I would like to offer it to you.

### Changes

* All files are .ts files now;
* I added types everywhere, so no more type complaints;
* I'm git-ignoring `.d.ts` and `.js` files in favor of `.ts` files only;
    * The change above forces the package generate the ignored files only when building, preferably when the package needs to be published.
* I updated all packages. They were somewhat outdated.

I did **NOT** check the tests. I think I tried to run it once, but that was it. Since I added types only (I didn't change any functionality), the tests should be good as well.

There might be some other changes, but I feel like the ones above are the main ones.

**Feel free to grab parts of it if you wish or ignore this PR. I didn't want to waste anybody's time in the future, in case you guys decide (one day, for some reason) to rewrite this nice lib in Typescript.**

Adds `StringInputWidget` component. Used in place of `TextWidget` as the default parameter widget when a parameter is not mapped to any fields. author: mina86
body:
Refactor `JsonRpcHandler::process_request_internal` method which is
one of the longest methods in our code base by:
- extracting common code into a new `process_method_call` function,
- moving adversarial requests handling to a new
  `process_adversarial_request_internal` method and
- creating separate methods for each type of adversarial RPC request.

This removes around 100 lines of code and reduces length of the method
from 325 lines to mere 88.

The `process_method_call` function is generic on the argument and
result of an RPC request.  It not only handles bunch of duplicated
code but thanks to type inference it also reduces amount of times the
same type needs to be specified.  The function is actually quite tiny,
but thanks to all the inference and syntax reduction it handles
replaces a few lines each time.

Similarly, introduce `serialize_response` which wraps a common call to
the serde serialisation.  Again, it’s a tiny function but the code it
replaces is a bit noisy so hopefully having a single method makes the
code more readable.

Lastly, `parse_params` was just a duplicate of function of the same
name from `api` module so just use that rather than duplicating the
code.  And observe that `jsonify` has always been called with
`Ok(Ok(value))` argument which means that it can be simplified to the
point where it’s not necessary.

author: vdubber
body:
## Purpose
The desired result of this change is to provide users an understanding of all possible steps available in an integration

## How?
Before a step is executed, the stepStartState is reference to see if the step is disabled. Prior to this change, if the step was disabled nothing would happen. Now, we add a job event log for the step indicating to the user that the step was disabled. Within the StepStartState, each step can be provided a reason for why it is disabled. It is the responsibility of the graph-* project to indicate why it was disabled. 

I believe this a positive change to exposing more information to the user about their integrations.
